title: Lee et al. 2019 (Motor Imagery) — EEG dataset and OpenBMI toolbox for three BCI paradigms: an investigation into BCI illiteracy
description: A comprehensive EEG dataset comprising 54 healthy subjects performing three major brain-computer interface (BCI) paradigms—motor imagery, event-related potentials, and steady-state visually evoked potentials—across two sessions. The dataset investigates BCI illiteracy rates and performance variations, revealing that motor imagery exhibits the highest illiteracy rate (53.7%) compared to other paradigms, while providing raw EEG recordings at 1000 Hz with 62 channels alongside auxiliary electromyography and resting-state data.
methods_description: EEG data were acquired from 54 healthy subjects (age 24-35 years) across two sessions using a 62-channel BrainAmp system with Ag/AgCl electrodes sampled at 1000 Hz, nose-referenced and grounded to AFz. Motor imagery trials consisted of 4-second periods of left or right hand grasping imagery cued by visual arrows, with 3-second preparation periods and 6-second inter-trial intervals. Each session included offline training and online test phases with 100 trials per paradigm. Impedance was maintained below 10 kOhm, and auxiliary recordings included 4-channel electromyography and artifact data.
